sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée regime), read together with Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. (registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); implemented through the INPI Guichet Unique pursuant to Décret n° 2023-160 of 26 February 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI — Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (single statutory online filing portal), with final RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract performed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within the jurisdiction of the company's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 — Déclaration d'immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accompanied by signed articles of association (statuts), capital-blocking attestation, legal-notice publication certificate, beneficial-owner declaration (DBE), and supporting identity and domiciliation dossiers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to a SAS (Article L.227-1 Code de commerce); capital is freely fixed in the articles, with a nominal low amount customary (e.g., EUR 1 to EUR 1,000). Any cash subscription must be deposited on an escrow suspense account ('compte de dépôt de fonds en attente') opened in the name of the company 'en formation' and remain blocked until RCS registration; the bank's attestation de blocage de fonds must accompany the M0 filing. In-kind contributions must be valued and annexed to the articles or, where statutory thresholds are exceeded, reviewed by a statutory contribution appraiser (commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the sole shareholder approves the full subscription of the issued share capital of [amount] euros, such funds being duly paid into a blocked suspense account with [bank] and evidenced by an escrow certificate issued in accordance with the Company's articles. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office is fixed at [address], France, within the registry district of [Commercial Court]. FURTHER RESOLVED that [name] is appointed President and [name] is appointed Managing Director, each with full authority to represent the Company and to sign all incorporation and banking documents; and that counsel is instructed to publish the legal announcement and file the incorporation dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Draft SAS Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI trade-name database (data.inpi.fr) / appointed French corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative name search against the INPI-RCS Register of Trade Names to confirm availability and preservation of the corporate name; instruct counsel to draft the statuts in French containing, at minimum: corporate object (online consignment and resale of second-hand luxury goods, ISIC 4791), registered-office domiciliation, fixed or variable share capital, President's appointment clause with optional general direction, share-transfer restrictions, and quorum/majority rules. Execute the statuts by each shareholder using a certified electronic signature or wet-ink signature; annex the domiciliation contract where the registered office is provided by a third party.
required_dossiers: Evidence of negative name search
Identity documents and passports of each shareholder and the President
Domiciliation contract or lease of registered office (if concluded)
CV of the President (voluntary)
Signed share-subscription schedule / capital allotment table
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals a conflicting mark, adjust the company name by adding distinguishing elements and re-run the search; if the registry queries a statutory clause, counsel redrafts the relevant article and the statuts are re-executed before continued filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution licensed by the ACPR (bank) or approved business-banking provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a transitory account in the name 'SAS [Company Name] en formation' and deposit the full subscribed cash capital. Request an officer of the bank to issue the attestation du dépositaire des fonds / attestation de blocage ('capital-blocking certificate') in compliance with Article R.227-2 of the Code de commerce, identifying the subscriber, the amount deposited, and the instruction that funds remain blocked until issuance of the Kbis. Where in-kind contributions exist, annex the contribution valuation report.
required_dossiers: Interim 'company under formation' status (letter of project)
Deposit order and payment proof
Identity of each subscriber
Contribution valuation deed (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to certify the blocking (e.g., pending sanctions checks), obtain a written refusal, engage an alternative licensed institute, or reduce capital to EUR 1 and treat the excess as shareholder current account (compte courant d'associé), then reissue the deposit deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Statutory Incorporation Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the JAL with the mandatory publication content: proposed corporate name, legal form (SAS), registered-office address, corporate object, amount of share capital, duration (default 99 years), identity of the President, and the registry office where the RCS file is to be opened. Ensure the notice is inserted after execution of the statuts and before the M0 filing; obtain the certificate of publication (certificat de parution) evidencing the precise insertion date.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice
Subscription order for the legal-announcement insertion
Final corporate name confirmation from the name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication certificate contains an error in company name or capital, request a free corrective republication from the JAL with the same publication date; after registry notice, refile the corrected certificate through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the M0 Incorporation Dossier through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI — Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit electronically the M0 form (déclaration de création / immatriculation) selecting 'SAS / Immatriculation au RCS'. Attach all required dossiers, pay the official filing fee online, and monitor the file status. The Guichet transmits the file to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, which creates the RCS entry. Respond to any 'pièce manquante' (missing document) request within 15 days through the same portal.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 registration form (online)
Signed final statuts
Attestation de blocage de fonds or in-kind contribution valuation report
Avis de constitution publication certificate from the JAL
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE) under Articles L.561-45 and L.561-46 of the Monetary and Financial Code
Déclaration de non-condamnation et de non-interdiction de gérer (BPN) of the President
Consent letters of officers accepting office
Proof of registered office (domiciliation contract, lease, or ownership deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is marked incomplete (A2 'en attente de pièces'), complete the electronic notice within 15 calendar days; if the name or domiciliation is contested, submit curative evidence to the registry and republish the notice where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract, SIREN/SIRET, and EU VAT Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI (Kbis and SIREN/SIRET), French tax office (VAT registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of incorporation, the registry delivers the first regular extract of the Kbis confirming legal existence. Verify all legal particulars, including the APE/NAF code attributed (expected 4791A / 4791B for distance-selling) and establishment location codes, then collect the SIREN (national identifier), SIRET (physical operational site), and the numéro de TVA intracommunautaire (EU VAT number). Apply for an EORI number if the company will directly import second-hand luxury items from outside the EU.
required_dossiers: Initial Kbis extract
Completed tax-office identification questionnaire
EORI application (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors (wrong NAF/APE or domiciliation), file a rectification request with the Greffe within 30 days or use the annual routine update; if VAT identification is delayed, contact the local tax office (pôle de conjoint) to expedite issuance of the EU VAT certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initialize Corporate Governance Books and Open Operating/Payment Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President / shareholder governance body; French banking and payment partners (Stripe, Escrow Pay)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the Kbis, convene and document the first shareholder decision approving the incorporation formalities; establish the statutory register of securities (registre d'actions) or the ledger of share movements; issue paper or electronic share documents where provided by the articles; open the company's operating bank account on presentation of the Kbis; submit the KYC/AML dossier to payment providers Stripe and Escrow Pay connecting a French merchant account denominated in euros; and complete the occupation notification for the registered business address.
required_dossiers: Final Kbis extract
Register of securities pages
Bank account documentation (AML/KYC)
Payment provider enhanced due-diligence waiver (KYC decision)
Vendor consignment agreements template for the luxury resale model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment partners defer approval on account of the medium-risk AML consignment classification, provide an enhanced due-diligence package comprising consignment agreements, source-of-goods declarations, sanctions checks, and historical transaction evidence; if the registry identifies unresolved corporate-governance issues, file curative minutes and amend the register accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — online consignment and second-hand luxury-goods retail under ISIC 4791 is an unlicensed commercial activity in France; the Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF) applies general consumer-code compliance rules, but no sectoral operating license is required. The Kbis extract constitutes the operating authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Kbis extract; no separate operating or manufacturing permit applies to the e-commerce resale model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — retail trade not otherwise listed under the Annex to Article R122-2 of the Code de l'environnement; no full EIA or environmental registration is mandated for a warehousing/showroom operation below ICPE declaration thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds apply. General compliance is required: French Circular Economy Law (loi AGEC) obligations for returns, waste sorting and traceability of disposed luxury goods; municipal waste collection arrangements; and a document unique d'évaluation des risques (DUER) covering occupational safety.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety — any showroom or boutique premises qualify as ERP type M, 5th category (under 300 m²), requiring a simple fire-prevention visitor's certificate and operational safety measures before opening; storage areas above ICPE thresholds (e.g., large-volume high-racking warehouses) would require a declaration or authorization from the prefecture. Workplace clearance under the Code du travail includes electrical installation verification (bilan de conformité), fire drills, first-aid equipment, and submission of the DUER to the occupational-health service; no civil-defense clearance is required for pure online retail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – impots.gouv.fr; company registration and tax ID procurement via Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must register with the French company formalities portal to obtain a SIREN/SIRET number. Where it has no permanent establishment in France but makes taxable supplies in France, it must separately register for French VAT with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). Non-EU entities generally must appoint a tax representative. VAT registration is evidenced by a French intra-community VAT number (FRXXXXXXXXX) and requires filing Form 1542-SD, supported by constitutional documents, foreign VAT status proof, and a description of French transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election exists in France. An SAS is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Certain partnerships may elect for corporate income tax, but an SAS has no such option. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are implemented and do not create elective neutralization mechanisms for an SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For an established French business selling goods (e.g., vintage luxury resale), the franchise en base exemption applies below €85,000 annual turnover, with a €93,500 tolerance; mandatory VAT registration is required once turnover exceeds the applicable threshold. A non-established foreign entity has no threshold and must register for French VAT as soon as it carries out any taxable supply in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is being phased in: from 1 September 2026 for large and medium enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small enterprises. E-invoices must be transmitted in a structured electronic format via a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). E-reporting of transaction data to the DGFiP is mandatory, with API/JSON structured formats specified. No fiscal stamping regime exists; the clearance mechanism relies on near-real-time structured data transmission to the State platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for the French VAT zero rate (exonération) under Article 262-I of the Code Général des Impôts where the goods are sold to an overseas buyer, physically leave French and EU customs territory, and are covered by a customs export declaration. Evidence must be retained proving irrevocable export within generally accepted deadlines (usually 90 days from supply). Intra-EU dispatches are exempt under Article 262-ter if the buyer holds a valid EU VAT number and the supplier files a recapitulative statement; they are not zero-rated for export. Distance sales to EU consumers are not export zero-rated and are instead subject to the OSS scheme where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU / ENS with MRN)
Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR)
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract or purchase order
Packing list and proof of export provenance
Inward remittance certificate or bank statement evidencing payment and FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated export zero-rating claims are reclassified by the DGFiP, triggering VAT reassessment plus interest de retard (0.20% per month). Deliberate inaccuracies attract a 40% bad-faith penalty under Article 1729 of the CGI; fraudulent schemes attract an 80% penalty and potential criminal prosecution. Retrospective clawback may extend over the standard 3-year tax limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud. Directors may also face personal liability and fines for participation in fraudulent zero-rating arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — central bank of the French Republic and the competent authority for monetary operations, balance-of-payments statistics, and cross-border financial reporting. The foreign exchange administration function is shared with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty) for foreign direct investment screening (régime IEF) under Articles L.151-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier, and with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential licensing and AML/CFT supervisory authority for credit institutions and Electronic Money Institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility. France, as a Eurozone member, applies Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union on the free movement of capital and payments and has abolished all exchange controls (Code monétaire et financier Art. L.151-1). The euro (EUR) is the sole legal tender. Current account transactions (commercial settlements, dividends, royalties, interest, commissions) and capital account transactions (equity contributions, shareholder loans, securities, real estate) are fully convertible without prior licensing or rationing. Profit remittance from a French SAS is unrestricted under French corporate law: dividends may be paid following the shareholders' meeting only if the distributable reserves exceed the share capital plus the legal reserve (Code de commerce Art. L.232-11), and the distribution is subject to the dividend withholding tax regime unless treaty relief applies. The remaining operational hurdles are (i) the mandatory intermediation of payments through a licensed credit institution or ACPR-licensed EMI (monopole bancaire) and (ii) statistical reporting to the Banque de France: the intermediary bank is obliged to capture the SAS's cross-border flows for the balance-of-payments survey when any single transaction reaches or exceeds EUR 750,000, and a direct-investment declaration is required where the inbound foreign investment meets the EUR 15,000,000 or 10% voting-rights threshold under the IEF regime. No administrative authorization applies to the profit distribution itself for a non-resident-owned SAS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable — no surrender regime exists. French and EU law impose no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds, whether derived from goods (vintage luxury resale) or services. The export proceeds may be freely retained in foreign currency on French or foreign bank accounts, and invoices may be denominated in any freely convertible currency. The only binding obligations are informational: (i) all export settlements must transit through a licensed financial intermediary (bank or, where technically permitted, an ACPR-licensed EMI); (ii) a cross-border flow equal to or exceeding EUR 750,000 in a single transaction (or aggregated flows to the same non-resident counterparty above the Banque de France reporting thresholds) must be captured in the balance-of-payments statistical survey via the intermediary bank; (iii) no exchange-control certificate or licence is required. Foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) are freely opened by the SAS with domestic banks, and conversion into EUR may be executed at market rates on a spot or forward basis.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (EUR/USD/GBP) plus regulated escrow account (compte séquestre) for consignment capital; merchant-collection sweep account
Operational EUR current account and cross-border treasury account with dedicated e-commerce KYC unit and SWIFT reporting
Operational account with direct USD/GBP clearing capacity via the HSBC global network and an FX hedging line
Operational account and merchant-receivables collection account
Operational account and fixed-deposit account for escrowed capital reserves
Wholesale treasury, correspondent banking, and OTC derivative clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: HIGH — with legal constraints. ACPR-licensed or EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) — Qonto, Shine, Treezor (Banking-as-a-Service), Mangopay (marketplace payout), and Wise Business — are fully viable for the operational euro rails of the luxury-resale SAS under Code monétaire et financier Art. L.521-1 et seq. and Art. L.525-4 (safeguarding of e-money in segregated accounts). Legal constraints: (1) the EMI must hold an ACPR licence or a valid EU passport; offshore and non-EEA EMIs cannot onboard the French SAS directly and must operate through a licensed partner bank; (2) an EMI may not open a true escrow account for third-party consignment funds beyond its safeguarded e-money model, and may not grant loans, issue letters of credit, or discount trade bills; (3) Stripe and Escrow_Pay settlement flows must be reconciled daily against the EMI or bank ledger; (4) the treasury policy should cap the e-money float held with any single EMI at EUR 1,000,000, with all excess balances swept automatically to the Tier-1 bank; (5) the recommended dual-rail architecture is a Tier-1 bank for capital/escrow and supplier documentary payments, an EMI for daily SEPA Instant collections and commission payouts, and Escrow_Pay as the buyer-facilitation escrow light intermediary for the platform transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an SAS carrying the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification, French Tier-1 banks operate under ACPR guidelines and Code monétaire et financier Art. L.561-5: they must identify the legal representatives and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs — any natural person controlling at least 25% of capital or voting rights). In practice, remote account opening is available at BNP Paribas, Société Générale, and HSBC Continental Europe for French or EU-resident presidents using eIDAS-compliant video KYC (ANSSI-certified), but the bank's compliance officer may require a physical interview at the head office or branch within 30 days given the enhanced-risk sector. For non-resident directors, physical presence of at least one managing director or of the appointed local representative is generally required, supported by: (i) an apostilled or legalized copy of the passport; (ii) a certified copy of the RCS Kbis extract issued within the prior three months; (iii) a banker's reference letter from the home-country financial institution confirming the director's good standing and source of wealth; (iv) an audited beneficial-ownership declaration. Where the presidency is held by another EU-resident corporate entity, remote video identification is generally sufficient.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque third-party consignors: the bank flags incoming secondhand luxury goods from multiple unrelated suppliers combined with payouts to non-contractual beneficiaries, triggering a trade-based money laundering (TBML) or fraudulent-consignment alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Standard consignment agreement (contrat de dépôt-vente) executed with each consignor; (2) vendor KYC file containing identity, professional RCS extraction, address, and tax identification; (3) goods provenance log (purchase receipts, serial numbers, and authentication certificates issued by Certilogo, Entrupy, or a recognized luxury-authentication house); (4) documentary trail of the Escrow_Pay account and the contractual purpose of every payout; (5) internal compliance manual evidencing a know-your-supplier program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value price inconsistency: sale of a single vintage lot above EUR 10,000 where market reference pricing is not verifiable, raising suspicion of over-invoicing, under-invoicing, or implicit value transfer via USD/GBP invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Independent third-party appraisal certificate per lot (commissioned expert or auction-house valuation); (2) comparable market sales data from recognized resale platforms (The RealReal, Vestiaire Collective, Christie's, Phillips); (3) documented internal price-band policy requiring a mandatory appraisal above EUR 5,000; (4) complete proof-of-sale record showing the customer's electronic checkout and authentication outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction counterparties: transfers from banks headquartered in FATF-listed or EU non-cooperative jurisdictions, or payments intermediated via digital-asset exchanges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Country-risk scoring matrix embedded in the treasury compliance policy; (2) source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, public-registry extracts) for each flagged remittance; (3) legalized or apostilled corporate documents of each flagged counterparty; (4) for digital-asset-origin funds, a certified blockchain-forensics report (Chainalysis or equivalent with risk score below the bank's threshold) and a declaration under Art. L.561-10 C. mon. fin.; (5) annual enhanced due diligence reviews of all non-EEA counterparts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between Stripe and Escrow_Pay merchant settlement reports and the MT940/MT942 bank statements (unexplained float, missed payouts, or manual journal entries), which the bank may interpret as concealment or misappropriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Written daily-reconciliation policy approved by the finance director; (2) monthly merchant-settlement reports (Stripe standard reconciliation files and Escrow_Pay payout history) mapped to bank account statements; (3) documented process for card refunds and chargeback handling; (4) ISAE 3402 or SOC 1 attestation report for Escrow_Pay as the external custodian; (5) quarterly treasury-adequacy letter issued by the statutory auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of funds and unsubstantiated shareholder loans: deposits from shareholders' personal accounts without documented equity or loan purpose, creating a bank risk classification of disguised distribution and potential fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Original equity-subscription certificates and the bank's certificate of funds deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds) for the initial capital; (2) formal shareholder current-account agreement (contrat de compte courant d'associé) stating principal, interest rate, duration, and repayment schedule; (3) the company's audited equity and debt schedule; (4) the consolidated shareholder register; (5) tax-legal documentation demonstrating compliance with the interest-deduction limits of Article 212 bis of the French General Tax Code and the recording of the loan in the annual statutory financial statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: (1) Share capital: the SAS's founders or the parent company subscribe by SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-resident subscribers or SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA subscribers; funds must be credited to a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the SAS 'en formation', held with the notary, a bank, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. The wire's Field 70 (Remittance Information) or the bank's purpose-code registry must bear the OECD/BPM6 purpose code 'EQSH — Equity Shares' or the French balance-of-payments category 'Investissements directs — prises de participation'. The depositary then issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds, which is filed at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce with the Kbis registration application. (2) Paid-in capital: although the SAS has no statutory minimum, a benchmark of EUR 50,000 is economically advisable to establish a viable merchant-acquiring limit and an acceptable bank risk score. An inbound foreign investment exceeding EUR 15,000,000 in aggregate, or carrying more than 10% of voting rights in a French target with turnover above EUR 25,000,000, requires an IEF declaration to the Direction Générale du Trésor (non-strategic retail sector); a EUR 50,000 injection is exempt. (3) Shareholder loans (comptes courants d'associés): the wire must use the BPM6 purpose code 'LI — Loans between direct investors'; a formal loan agreement must specify principal, EUR interest rate, duration, and repayment schedule, with the interest rate not exceeding the French usury ceiling (Art. L.314-1 C. conso.) to avoid reclassification as a disguised distribution. (4) Verification: each inbound wire must match the remitter against the signed shareholder register, and the beneficiary bank must complete compliance review of the Kbis extract, the UBO declaration, and the board resolution authorizing the capital increase or loan. (5) Any inbound financing from a non-EEA parent must be denominated in EUR, USD, or GBP and is eligible for the treasury ring-fenced liquidity pool, with the intent recorded in the board minutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (a) EU supplier payments — SEPA Credit Transfer executed via the ISO 20022 pain.001.001.03 message with purpose code 'GOOD' (purchase/sale of goods), using SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for same-second settlement up to EUR 100,000 where the supplier's bank is reachable, otherwise standard SEPA CT with same-day or D+1 settlement; (b) non-EU supplier payments — SWIFT MT103 wire transfer routed through the correspondent-bank network (CHIPS or Fedwire for USD, CHAPS for GBP, TARGET2 for EUR), with purpose code 'MRCH' or 'GOOD' and the beneficiary bank identified by SWIFT BIC; (c) high-value or documentary transactions above EUR 100,000 — Commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700, with the French bank as issuing bank and the foreign supplier's bank negotiating against the shipping documents and authentication certificates; (d) customer refunds and card chargebacks — routed through Stripe's card network (Visa/Mastercard) using an explicit refund reference, and via SEPA CT for bank-to-bank refunds; (e) consignor payouts — under the Escrow_Pay model, the escrow provider collects buyer funds and disburses to the SAS upon delivery confirmation, after which the SAS pays each consignor its net commission by SEPA CT on a T+1 basis; the bank requires a monthly consignor-payout register demonstrating the commercial rationale for every beneficiary; (f) all outbound disbursements must be pre-funded in the dedicated operational account to avoid overdraft, and the treasury policy sets a maximum outgoing exposure of EUR 1,000,000 per counterparty per month.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Outright Forwards — OTC with ACPR-authorized banks, documented under an ISDA 2002 French-law master agreement or the bank's standard dealing terms; maturities up to 12 months; the SAS as an end-user is exempt from EMIR mandatory clearing below the EUR 8 billion gross notional threshold, but every trade must be reported to a registered trade repository (e.g., DTCC Data Repository or UnaVista).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permitted for restricted or exotic currencies (e.g., offshore CNY, KRW, INR) with full cash settlement in EUR or USD at maturity, executed under the bank's standard NDF terms and margin requirements.

Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) — for matched funding of a USD or GBP working-capital pool, exchanging EUR floating-rate (€STR) against USD SOFR or GBP SONIA on a quarterly basis; generally available for notional amounts from EUR 5,000,000 and used to hedge balance-sheet exposure from the cross-border inventory acquisition pipeline.

Vanilla European FX Options (Call/Put) — OTC premium-bearing strategies, including simple or zero-cost collars, to cap adverse EUR/USD and EUR/GBP moves on anticipated receivables; execution requires an ISDA Credit Support Annex (CSA) for margining or an upfront cash-collateral arrangement.

FX Spot and Overnight Swap — same-day or T+2 settlement executed through the corporate bank's FX desk under an FX Master Agreement, used for the daily conversion of multi-currency settlement balances into EUR and for managing short-term liquidity in the operational account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) - Form 2065 and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) via professional e-filing portal (EDI/EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entities: by the 2nd working day after 1 May (paper) or the 3rd working day after 1 May (e-filed EDI/EFI); non-calendar year entities: within 3 months of fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed tax; escalation to 40% if unpaid within 30 days of formal notice and 80% for intentional concealment; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of the statutory financial statements by the sole shareholder or shareholders' meeting (decision d'affectation du résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records; executed decision is annexed to the RCS annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year close (e.g., by 30 June 2025 for a 31 December 2024 year-end); any shareholder may petition the court to order the meeting if the statutory deadline is missed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered meeting at company expense; the missing approval blocks the greffe filing and triggers the registrar's strike-off notification chain.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit to the Trade and Companies Register (dépôt des comptes annuels) with management report and auditor's report if any
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of accounts approval and in all cases before the 7-month anniversary of fiscal year close (e.g., 31 July 2025 for a calendar-year SAS); confidentiality option for the income statement under Code de commerce L.232-25 is exercised at filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from the greffe; court president may impose a civil fine up to €3,000 and a coercive daily fine up to €90; persistent non-filing beyond one year triggers administrative radiation from the RCS with loss of separate legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration review and update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS (INPI Guichet Unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No stand-alone annual filing if the beneficial ownership structure is unchanged; any direct or indirect ownership or control change must be filed within 30 days; annual accuracy is re-confirmed at the accounts approval meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €15,000 for natural persons and €75,000 for legal persons for failure to file or false declaration (Code monétaire et financier L.561-33); court order may compel compliance and the RCS remarks the register until updated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) business premises declaration and annual payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP - local corporate and property tax offices (SIE / service des impôts fonciers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration on Form 1447-C-SD within 2 months of business commencement (new premises declaration follows the same rule); no re-filing required in years without changes; CFE tax rolls are payable in two instalments on 15 June and 15 December, or in full on the December balance for assessments under €3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 10% plus interest of 0.20% per month on overdue amounts; enforced recovery via tax warrant (avis de mise en recouvrement); no strike-off impact.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a certified statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when the SAS exceeds at least two of the three thresholds at year-end: balance sheet total above €4,000,000; net turnover (excluding VAT) above €8,000,000; average of 50 or more employees during the period; group/subsidiary relationships and specific court orders may also trigger audit. The medium-risk AML profile of the vintage luxury resale platform does not in itself compel an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP as codified in ANC Regulation 2014-03 (Plan Comptable Général); individual statutory accounts of a French SAS must be prepared in Euros and in French; IFRS is reserved for consolidated financial statements and is not mandatory for a standalone SAS; simplified presentation may apply to small entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial ownership register is filed at the RCS at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any share transfer, option exercise or control change; the annual accounts approval meeting is the mandatory calendar checkpoint at which the compliance function must reconcile the share-ledger transfers, update the DBE file if ownership changed, and verify that the senior management declarations remain accurate. The escrow and consignment settlement structure should not hold legal title to the goods or shares without a mirror RCS entry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities Movements (Registre des mouvements de titres) - share transfer ledger
Minutes and Decisions Register (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux) - sole shareholder or shareholders' meetings
Beneficial Owners Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) - internal copy of the RCS central file
Police Register for secondhand luxury goods (Registre de police / revendeur d'objets mobiliers) - consignment intake, description and vendor identity log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200-$700 (approx. €180-€650) per year for a professional domicile or registered office in France; premium commercial addresses in Paris raise the upper bound to about $1,200.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500-$10,000 (approx. €3,200-€9,200) per year for a statutory audit by a commissaire aux comptes when thresholds are exceeded; a voluntary limited review (examen limité) generally costs $2,000-$4,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced CIT rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit per FY for eligible SMEs (turnover < €10,000,000); R&D tax credit (CIR) — not applicable to resale; Innovation tax credit (CII); no special regime for online resale.
